description: A General History of the Robberies and Murders of the most notorious Pyrates is a 1724 book containing biographies of contemporary pirates. It's author uses the name Captain Charles Johnson, generally considered a pseudonym. The real identity of the author was thought by some scholars to be Daniel Defoe, although this has since been disputed. The publisher Nathaniel Mist or somebody working for him are other suggested authors. In the first volume, "Johnson" sticks fairly close to the available sources, though he embellishes the stories somewhat. Nevertheless, the book was influential in shaping popular notions of piracy and provided the standard account of the lives of many individuals still famous in the 21st century.(Summary by Wikipedia)

In the present volume the author has endeavored to trace the evolution of the different industries, and to describe in everyday language the methods of manufacture in our principle industries. title: Spanish Tragedy

description: The Spanish Tragedy, or Hieronimo is Mad Again is an Elizabethan tragedy written by Thomas Kyd between 1582 and 1592. Highly popular and influential in its time, The Spanish Tragedy established a new genre in English theatre, the revenge play or revenge tragedy. Its plot contains several violent murders and includes as one of its characters a personification of Revenge. (Thomas Kyd is frequently proposed as the author of the hypothetical Ur-Hamlet that may have been one of Shakespeare's primary sources for Hamlet.) title: Sonnets
author: Edna St. Vincent Millay
description: It has been observed that within the narrow confines of a sonnet the mind can turn around but cannot take flight. Some of Millay’s sonnets, though, resemble the narrow confines of a loaded pistol (with a silencer), at the end of which the reader feels propelled to a higher emotional plane. Nevertheless, the predominant mood is melancholy, regret for the brevity of life and especially for the death of her husband. Today’s world can accept more readily than her own the feminism of her poetry and her casual but touching references to love outside of marriage. Millay’s syntax can become challenging, but her most profound utterances are simply phrased (“I do not think I would”) and often startlingly colloquial: “you may whistle for me.” Millay does not follow exclusively the Shakespearean or the Italian rhyme scheme in her sonnets but varies at will. Her iambic meter is (except as indicated below) as strict as Milton’s, with the same love of enjambment and inverted feet to obscure rhymes and to create bouncing rhythms and sudden turns. Her handling of the sonnet form departs rarely but sometimes radically from tradition, as when a heptameter line (of seven feet) replaces the pentameter at the end of a sonnet, a regular feature of the final lines of “Sonnets from an Ungrafted Tree”; e.g., “And some old catalogue, and a brown, shriveled apple core.” She also permits an extrametrical weak syllable at the caesura and occasional other weak, nearly negligible syllables elsewhere, usually justified as pronounceable elisions, like “risen” (ris’n), “blossoming” (bloss’ming), “enemy” (en’my); yet sometimes not, like “ne(ver),” “ult(i)mate,” “flat(tened).” (Summary by T. A. Copeland)

title: Andromache
author: Euripides
description: Andromache is a Classical Greek verse tragedy written by Euripides in the 5th century BCE. When Troy was taken by the Greeks, Andromache, wife of that Hector whom Achilles slew ere himself was slain by the arrow which Apollo guided, was given in the dividing of the spoils to Neoptolemus, Achilles’ son. So he took her oversea to the land of Thessaly, and loved her, and entreated her kindly, and she bare him a son in her captivity. But after ten years! Neoptolemus took to wife a princess of Sparta, Hermione, daughter of Menelaus and Helen. But to these was no child born, and the soul of Hermione grew bitter with jealousy against Andromache. Now Neoptolemus, in his indignation for his father’s death, had upbraided Apollo therewith: wherefore he now journeyed to Delphi, vainly hoping by prayer and sacrifice to assuage the wrath of the God. But so soon as he was gone, Hermione sought to avenge herself on Andromache ; and Menelaus came thither also, and these twain went about to slay the captive and her child, Wherefore Andromache hid her son, and took sanctuary at the altar of the Goddess Thetis, expecting till Peleus, her lord’s grandsire, should come to save her. And herein are set forth her sore peril and deliverance : also it is told how Neoptolemus found death at Delphi, and how he that contrived his death took his wife. (Summary by Alan Mapstone and the Translator) Cast List Andromache: Wendy Katz Hiller Handmaid: Agnes Robert Behr Hermione: Rita Boutros Menelaus: Algy Pug Molossus: Inkell Peleus: Beeswaxcandle Nurse: Sonia Orestes: Greg Giordano Messenger: Larry Wilson Thetis: dc Chorus: Alan Mapstone Stage Directions: James R Hedrick

description:
Welcome to the Soft Season with LWB, a sacred space created to honor the rest, healing, and inner wisdom of Black women. For generations, Black women have carried families, communities, and cultures, often placing the needs of others before their own. Studies continue to show that the overwhelming majority of Black women experience chronic stress, making intentional rest not a luxury, but a vital act of restoration. This channel exists as an invitation to return to yourself. These guided meditations are lovingly created for Black women embracing their soft season, a season of stillness, self-reflection, emotional healing, and radical self-love. Here, softness is strength. Rest is resistance. Healing is inheritance. Each meditation honors the ancestral women who walked before us, whose resilience, prayers, and love live within us today. We also meditate for the generations yet to come, for our daughters, nieces, granddaughters, and every young Black girl who deserves to inherit peace alongside power. This is a place to reconnect with your breath, your body, your spirit, and your purpose. To release what no longer serves you. To remember that your worth has never been defined by how much you carry or how tirelessly you give. Black women have always been among humanity's greatest nurturers, creators, visionaries, and healers. These meditations celebrate that enduring legacy while making space for something equally sacred: your own well-being. May each practice bring you closer to peace, deeper into yourself, and back to the softness that has always been yours. 

Welcome home sis. 
We love you, we've got you, we are you!

title: Selected Poems
author: George Herbert
description: These poems, from Herbert’s book The Temple, show the evolution of a soul’s relationship with God. Sudden reversals of mood are common, for although Herbert is best known for his quiet tone, he was not a tranquil man but proud and ambitious. He achieved tranquility by active effort. His works may be read autobiographically, for they are intensely personal. Yet through his personal experience we perceive a reality larger than the personal. For example, his many homely comparisons—to bowling, pulleys, laxatives, a blunted knife, sweeping a room—serve “for lights of Heavenly Truths,” as he says of scriptural references to matters of daily life like “a plough, a hatchet, leaven, boyes piping and dancing.” Hence we find in Herbert a startling simplicity of spirit, an almost mystical ability to make every sensory experience sacramental and to express deep and subtle emotions with perfect tact. But there are also angry, frustrated, nearly despairing moments when he longs for the worldly paths he might have taken, the academic honors, the seat in Parliament that he once held, “the ways of Pleasure, the sweet strains, / The lullings and the relishes of it.” But at such moments God is always at hand to throw him a lifeline—whispering in his ear, recalling him to a far deeper and older level of emotional experience. (summary by T. A. Copeland)

title: Someone to Watch Over Me: A Journey Through Hyperspace
author: H. L. Gold & Floyd C. Gale
description:
Len Mattern stumbles into a cosmic nightmare when he discovers the terrifying truth about hyperspace. In this gripping science fiction audiobook, listeners join Len on a harrowing journey where the laws of reality twist and turn, challenging everything he knows about existence. As he navigates the treacherous expanse of hyperspace, Len grapples with an unsettling conflict: the very fabric of time and space is unraveling, and he holds the key to either its salvation or destruction.

With the fate of countless lives hanging in the balance, Len must confront sinister forces that lurk in the void, all while racing against time to unlock the secrets hidden within hyperspace. What drives him? A haunting promise to protect those he loves, even as the line between ally and enemy blurs in this otherworldly dimension.

Through vivid storytelling and thought-provoking themes, 'Someone to Watch Over Me' explores the nature of sacrifice, the essence of heroism, and the shadows that haunt our choices. Each twist and turn reveals deeper layers of mystery that will keep you guessing until the very end. Can Len outsmart the unseen adversaries that threaten his mission? Or will he become a lost soul in the depths of the unknown? This audiobook invites you to ponder the limits of our understanding and the courage it takes to confront the impossible.

title: Something In Between's Podcast

Welcome to Somewhere In Between.

Somewhere In Between is a podcast for parents who are rediscovering themselves while raising their children.

Whether you're a mom, a dad, a stay-at-home parent, a working parent, or somewhere in between, this is a space for honest conversations about identity, ambition, ADHD, creativity, career, relationships, and everything that comes with trying to build a life you love while raising someone else.

This isn't a parenting podcast filled with expert advice.

It's a place where we talk openly about the messy, beautiful, and often complicated journey of becoming yourself again.

Every week, you'll find conversations about:
 ✨ Parenthood & identity
 ✨ ADHD & the creative mind
 ✨ Building a business or career after kids
 ✨ Mental load & mom/dad guilt
 ✨ Personal growth
 ✨ Finding balance

If you've ever wondered...

"Who am I outside of being a parent?"

Subscribe and join the journey.

title: The Gloved Hand: A Midnight Mystery
author: Burton Egbert Stevenson
description:
Private investigator Mr. Lester never expected a simple case to lead him to a midnight spectacle of otherworldly proportions. While visiting a sprawling country estate, he and his friend Godfrey witness a mysterious 'falling star' that ignites the night sky above two figures draped in white robes. One of them is a young woman, and her connection to the strange occurrence plunges them into a web of secrets and intrigue.

As they delve deeper, Lester and Godfrey uncover layers of deception that intertwine the estate's past with a series of bizarre events. Who are these enigmatic figures? What secrets does the estate hold? With each new twist, the stakes rise, and the duo must navigate the complexities of loyalty, love, and betrayal.

'Gloved Hand' spins a tale that blends mystery with a touch of the supernatural, inviting listeners to ponder the thin line between reality and the extraordinary. Join Lester and Godfrey as they unravel a case that challenges everything they believe about the world around them. Will they solve the mystery before it’s too late? Tune in to experience the suspense, and perhaps uncover something extraordinary within yourself.

Each exhibits the vigorous exactness, and the mixture of realism and romanticism, for which Flaubert is renowned.

title: Our Little Macedonian Cousin: A Journey Through Ancient Macedon
author: Julia Darrow Cowles
description:
When young Arete discovers a mysterious artifact buried near her village, she unwittingly unravels a web of secrets that could change the fate of ancient Macedon forever. In 'Our Little Macedonian Cousin of Long Ago,' Julia Darrow Cowles immerses listeners in the heart of a rugged culture where loyalty, bravery, and the echoes of battlefield glory shape everyday life.

As Arete navigates her childhood against the backdrop of a society famed for its warriors and leaders, each day presents new challenges, whether it’s mastering her spear skills or deciphering the whispers of the elders. With her playful spirit and sharp wit, Arete embarks on a journey filled with friendship, rivalry, and the heavy weight of expectations.

While she learns the ways of her ancestors, Arete also grapples with the pressures of her destiny. Will she fulfill her family's legacy, or will the truths she uncovers lead her to question everything she knows? This captivating story beautifully intertwines themes of courage, identity, and the quest for knowledge, drawing listeners into a world where history and imagination collide. Join Arete as she transforms from a curious child into a fierce guardian of her people, and discover the fascinating history that shaped one of the greatest civilizations of all time.

title: Better Do Than Don’t!
author: Matan Hirschhorn
description:
Better Do Than Don't is the podcast for doers. Hosted by a serial entrepreneur who owns multiple
businesses, closes deals and finds clarity on the golf course — his office — and spends his free time
on the youth baseball field with his kids. We talk business, AI, and life. Real conversations. Real
people. No excuses.

Matan has been building businesses his whole life — not because it was the plan, but because sitting still was never
really an option. One business turned into many, and somewhere along the way the journey became just as
addictive as the destination. Today he runs multiple companies and is always quietly scouting the next opportunity,
the next industry, the next conversation that sparks something new.
For Matan, networking isn't a strategy — it's a way of life. He genuinely believes that the right connection at the
right moment can change everything, and he has built his career on that belief. If he could spend every day meeting
business owners, sharing ideas, and helping people find their next move — he would. This podcast is pretty much
exactly that.
When the work day is done you'll find him on the back nine or on the youth baseball field watching and coaching
his kids play ball.
Better Do Than Don't is his philosophy and now his podcast. Because waiting until you're ready is just another way
of never starting.

title: Second Chances: The Best Parts are on Side B
author: Jennie K. Drollinger
description:
Second Chances: The Best Parts are on Side B

Have you ever wondered, “Did I miss my chance?”

Hosted by Jennie K. Drollinger—an unapologetic ’80s girl at heart—Second Chances is a storytelling podcast about second chances in love, career, health, family, faith, purpose, and life after unexpected change.

Each episode shares real, hope-filled stories of people who found their Side B: rekindled romances, love after divorce, restored marriages, career reinvention, health recovery, healing after heartbreak, family reconnection, and new beginnings after loss, failure, or fear.

It all began with Jennie’s own lost and found love story: meeting a boy in H.S. 1985 Alaska, falling fast, then losing touch through misunderstandings and an old-school disconnected landline—a mystery that took over three decades to explain and finally uncover what really happened. Thirty years later, they found their way back to each other. Their journey captured hearts nationwide and was crowned America’s Favorite Couple 2025, winning out of 210,000 couples.

But this isn’t just a love story podcast. It’s a community of Side B moments—a place for listeners to share stories of resilience, forgiveness, healing, personal growth, reinvention, purpose, and proof that it’s never too late to begin again.

Pull up a chair. Get cozy. You’re not too late.

"Your life didn’t end when your plans did—some stories aren’t over yet, and the best parts may still be waiting on Side B."

Your Side B story could give someone hope!

title: From Probe to Practice
author: Advanced Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Center
description:
From Probe to Practice is a weekly podcast on musculoskeletal
    ultrasound — diagnostic scanning, ultrasound-guided injections, and how
    MSK ultrasound changes the way clinicians practice regenerative and
    musculoskeletal medicine.

    Hosted by Colin Rigney and Ryan Martin, founders of the Advanced MSK
    Ultrasound Center, who have trained clinicians for years and bring the
    reps to prove it.

    This is not a 45-minute monologue on probe physics. It's a high-energy
    dialogue about what actually happens inside a practice: the diagnostic
    gaps nobody mentions, the injections that miss and why, the referrals
    you didn't need to make, the business of integrating ultrasound, and
    the case studies that only come from tens of thousands of scans. Plus,
    in Ryan's words, "a lot of dirt on each other."

    Every episode is built around one promise: take something you learned
    from a podcast on Friday and implement it on Monday.

    For physicians, regenerative medicine clinicians, sports medicine
    providers, anyone preparing for the RMSK exam — and anyone who works
    alongside them.

    Because you can't diagnose what you can't see.

    New episodes weekly. An Advanced MSK Ultrasound Center podcast.

description: You care about climate change. You're just not sure your choices actually matter. Climate, Actually is here to show you they do, and exactly how to use them. Together they work through the facts, sit with the feelings that come with facing the crisis, and land on one clear action you can take too. If your income puts you in the world's top 10% of earners (it starts lower than you'd think), your choices carry outsized climate weight. This show helps you use that weight well.

title: Reflections: Web Security Podcast
author: Reflectiz
description:
Reflections: The Web Security Podcast is produced by Reflectiz, the world's leading AI-powered web exposure platform. Built by world renowned ethical hackers, Reflectiz continuously monitors everything executing on your live website - detecting the threats that firewalls, WAFs, and traditional scanners were never designed to see.
Each episode, we sit down with security practitioners, CISOs, privacy officers, and compliance experts to examine the threats reshaping the modern web and what organizations can actually do about them.
What We Cover:
Magecart attacks, web skimming, and checkout page security
Third-party script risk and unauthorised data exfiltration
PCI DSS 4.0.1 compliance for merchants and payment providers
GDPR, CCPA, and HIPAA enforcement at the client-side layer
AI-generated web attacks and evolving supply-chain compromises
Fourth-party risk and what lives beyond your engineering control
Real breach post-mortems and actionable takeaways for security teams
Who It's For:
Reflections is essential listening for CISOs, AppSec engineers, privacy and compliance managers, and security-conscious leaders across financial services, e-commerce, healthcare, and the public sector.
Subscribe, reflect, and stay ahead of the web threats your current stack can't see.

title: God’s Receptionist
author: godsreceptionistpodcast
description:
God’s Receptionist is a judgment-free space for women to pause in the middle of busy lives and reconnect with who they truly are in Christ. In a world that defines us by titles—mother, wife, professional, daughter—this podcast gently reminds us that before anything else, we are first a child of God.
This is not a place for perfection or expertise. Kristy is not a theologian, intellectual, or spiritual expert—she is simply a mom, wife, and woman of faith who has been where you are, or is walking through it right alongside you. This space exists not to teach from a pedestal, but to learn, grow, and seek God together as students of the Word.
Kristy shares spiritual lessons gathered from trusted faith leaders, cross-referenced with Scripture, and tested in the trenches of everyday life. Together, we explore who God is, what He has said, and how His truth shapes our identity.
Whether we’re diving into biblical foundations or having honest conversations about motherhood, marriage, womanhood, and life’s challenges, this podcast is a safe place for women of faith to grow spiritually without judgment. Here, we don’t just manage the “calls” of daily life—we learn to recognize the voice of the One who called us first.
What we explore together:
Biblical Foundations to anchor your faith
Identity Beyond Titles, reminding us we are daughters of the King
Honest Life Conversations rooted in grace, truth, and growth
Thank you for being here, for listening, and for choosing to grow closer to God alongside us. You are seen, you are welcome, and you belong here.

title: You've Got People Problems
author: Melissa Ortiz, Talent Optimization Expert
description:
Let’s be honest. People problems aren’t just HR problems. They’re business problems.


They show up as missed goals, unclear accountability, hiring mistakes, disengaged teams, and leaders carrying more than they should. Over time, they slow growth, create frustration, and make running a business feel harder than it needs to be. And they aren’t solved by another policy, personality test, or quick fix.

Business would be simple… if it weren’t for people.


That’s the reality behind You’ve Got People Problems, a podcast focused on the human side of running a business. Each episode explores how leadership behavior, hiring decisions, role clarity, engagement, and organizational structure directly impact performance, culture, and results.


Through honest conversations with business owners, operators, HR leaders, EOS Implementers, and consultants, the show tackles real issues leaders face every day: why the “right hire” still isn’t working, how teams outgrow roles, when full-time isn’t the answer, why accountability breaks down, and what actually drives engagement beyond perks and pay.


This isn’t about HR checking a box or leadership theory. It’s about helping leaders slow down, recognize patterns earlier, and make more intentional people decisions that support both the business and the people inside it.


If you’re leading a team, building an organization, or trying to get out of the day-to-day firefighting that comes with people problems, this podcast is for you.

Subscribe, listen, and start making sense of the people side of your business.

title: Venus and Adonis (Version 2)
author: William Shakespeare
description: Both Ovid and Spenser also treat this ancient myth, but Spenser alters the ending, converting the tale into an archetype of fulfilled love, whereas Ovid, like Shakespeare, combines humor with pathos as a buffer against sentimentality. Ovid’s Venus behaves absurdly out of character, becoming a huntress to keep her lover company in the woods. Shakespeare, however, preserves decorum; his Venus remains at all times the queen of love. The humor arises rather from the fact that the would-be paramour isn’t interested. This endows the goddess’s wooing with nearly slapstick over-exertion, and yet her sincerity makes her appealing, while Adonis’s immaturity forces us to respect his chastity. The pathos comes, of course, from the unhappy ending—more unhappy because we do not expect a comedy to end sadly, especially not when we sympathize with the characters. The poetic form or genre, the epyllion, is an erotic narrative based on mythology, like Marlowe's Hero and Leander and, later, Phineus Fletcher's Venus and Anchises, also found in the Librivox catalogue. Venus and Adonis and The Rape of Lucrece, both narrative poems, are the only works that Shakespeare ever carefully saw through the press. - Summary by T. A. Copeland

title: That Salty Girl: Confidence, Reinvention, And Figuring Out What's Next
author: Holly Taylor: Navy Veteran, Entrepreneur, Mentor
description:
You don’t have to have it figured out to start.


After spending 26 years in the Navy, followed by a stretch in corporate America, Holly Taylor found herself starting over again in her 50s, this time, building a business from scratch. That business became The Salty Spray, a mobile spray-tanning company. If you’d told her at 18 that this would be her path, she probably wouldn’t have believed you. And that’s the whole point of this show.


When Holly retired from the Navy, the transition was harder than anyone had warned her it would be. What helped her through wasn’t advice or a perfect roadmap. It was hearing from people who had already been through it. People who reminded her that what she was feeling was normal. Now, she wants to be that person for you.


Most weeks, you’ll hear directly from Holly, talking to you the way she would talk to a friend at her kitchen table. No five-step formulas. Just honest conversations about starting over, rebuilding confidence, rediscovering your identity after a big change, and navigating that stuck, in-between feeling of not knowing what comes next.


Some weeks, she’ll introduce you to someone in the middle of a reinvention of their own; a client, a friend, or someone standing right where you might be now.


Through the women Holly tans in their own homes and the people who unexpectedly find their way into her DMs, she hears versions of the same story again and again. The woman ready to leave corporate for good and finally work for herself. The woman rebuilding her life after a divorce. Different ages. Different circumstances. But underneath it all is the same quiet question: Is it too late for me?


Holly’s answer is simple: it’s not.


You don’t need to have the entire path mapped out. You just have to be willing to take the next step before you feel ready.

Whatever’s next, you’re not behind.


Subscribe and listen to a new episodes every week. Also, join Holly’s newsletter, The Salty Scoop, for personal stories, photos, and pieces of life she doesn’t share anywhere else!

description: In the Dark, hosted by Madeleine Baran, is an award-winning investigative-journalism podcast that started in 2016. Its first season looked at the mysterious abduction of Jacob Wetterling in rural Minnesota and the lack of accountability that sheriffs face when they fail to solve cases. Season 2 examined the case of Curtis Flowers, who was tried six times for the same crime. In 2020, In the Dark released a special report on the coronavirus pandemic in the Mississippi Delta. In 2023, In the Dark joined The New Yorker and in 2024, it released “The Runaway Princesses,” a four-part series that asks why the women in Dubai’s royal family keep trying to run away. Season 3, released in 2024, asked why no one was punished for the killings of twenty-five civilians in Haditha, Iraq. In the Dark won the Pulitzer Prize for audio for Season 3. The podcast is a three-time Peabody Award winner and, in 2019, became the first podcast to win a George Polk Award, one of the top honors in journalism. The program has also received an Alfred I. duPont-Columbia University Award and a Robert F. Kennedy Journalism Award. New Yorker subscribers get early, ad-free access. In Apple Podcasts, tap the link at the top of the feed to subscribe or link an existing subscription. title: Episode 26.82 - The Birth of a Pheonix

description:

Guest Amber Fourman. 
Amber will share her experiences with gender incongruence, gender dysphoria, and her journey into and through Gender Affirmation resulting in the Birth of a Pheonix  

Episode 26.83
Explorative Deep Diver into Gender and Sexual Minority Resilience  

Paradoxes of Gender Podcasts:
The Paradoxes of Gender Podcasts are Designed to Deliver Professional Development Educational Programs for the LGBTQ+ Medical & Behavioral Healthcare Providers who provide Medical & Behavioral Healthcare Services to Transgender, Gender Diverse, Gender Non-Conforming, Gender Incongruent and Non-Binary Individuals.  

Prepared & Presented by:
Dr. Diana Sorrentino, Ph.D. Social-Psychologist & Behavioral Analyst  

Delivering comprehensive Medical or Behavioral Healthcare Services as a component of your practice on behalf of Transgender (TG), Gender Diverse (GD) Individuals and members of the LGBTQ+ Community may at times prove to be a little challenging. The challenges you may experience have historically been caused by a lack of specialized medical or behavioral health training you received in preparation for your career and the care you will be providing for Transgender and Gender Diverse patients.   

This understanding was underscored and reinforced by a 2011 study, reported in the Journal of the American Medical Association, the medical schools, on average, only provide Five (5) hours of academic or clinical instruction on LGBTQ+ healthcare requirements.  In the absence of specialized training; time is required to acquire first-hand real-world knowledge and experience with the diverse challenges, needs and experiences these individuals present and what they are confronted with as they live their lives in their Self-Attributed Non-Conforming Gender roles.  

Transgender, Gender Diverse, Gender Non-Conforming, Gender Incongruent & Non-Binary individuals, their families, friends, schools, employers and social-networks will also benefit from the content of these Podcasts in-spite of the fact that the detailed medical and psychological content of these programs focuses on the continuing educational needs and requirements of the medical or behavioral healthcare professional.  Knowledge is essential to counteract the negative publicity and the political hyperbole disseminated by individuals with no understanding of the history and underlying biological factors influencing gender non-conformity.

The Millbrook Files is an investigative horror podcast following independent podcaster Avery Quinn as she sets out to document the strange folklore surrounding one forgotten small town. Urban legends. Haunted locations. Unexplained disappearances. Forgotten cemeteries. Scary stories everyone swears happened to a friend of a friend.


Then a package arrives.


Inside: a weathered red binder labeled The Campfire Protocols, a collection of bizarre rules supposedly written by the people responsible for patrolling Blackwood Forest. Rules that make no sense... until listeners begin recognizing them, strangers start warning Avery to stop asking questions, and people begin remembering the town differently.


This is not a ghost story. This is evidence.


Presented as a real investigative podcast recorded in real time, The Millbrook Files is a serialized audio drama horror experience. Every episode is another piece of a conspiracy you were never supposed to uncover. Records disappear, witnesses change their stories, entire places vanish from history. And somewhere in the background of every investigation, watching from just beyond the edge of the frame, is a silent figure known only as The Man in the Hat.


Some stories are meant to be told….Others were buried for a reason.


New episodes drop every week. Subscribe and follow the investigation from the beginning.


START FROM FILE 001 — I Live in the Weirdest Town in America 


If you love found footage horror, paranormal investigation, small town horror mysteries, creepypasta, or audio drama horror with a conspiracy edge this is your playlist.

 The Millbrook Files is horror storytelling crafted by humans, presented as if it's real. No jump scares. No gimmicks. Just a case file that keeps getting harder to close.


Avery Quinn is not responsible for what you remember after listening.

As one of the original members of 600, he witnessed the rise of the movement, the success, and the devastating losses that defined that generation.

This podcast isn’t about glorifying violence or reliving the past—it’s about honest conversations, accountability, growth, and speaking on real-life experiences from someone who has lived them.

Expect unfiltered discussions on music, sports, relationships, current events, prison life, street culture, and whatever else is worth talking about. Some episodes will feature call-ins from listeners, while others will include guests and open conversations with people from all walks of life.

The goal is simple: keep it real, make people think, have some laughs, and show that growth is possible. Your past may explain where you came from, but it doesn’t have to define where you’re going.

Welcome to All the Things They Said — where nothing is off-limits and every question is fair game.
Inspired by the iconic format of 1 Girl 5 Gays, this is our unfiltered, chaotic, and sometimes too-honest take on life, dating, friendships, pop culture, and everything in between.
Each episode, Jenn comes in hot with 20 questions… and Gen answers like his life depends on it.
Expect:
Brutal honesty
Unhinged opinions
Questionable advice
And way too much oversharing
If you’ve ever wondered what someone really thinks… you’re in the right place.

title: The Law Queen Podcast
author: thelawqueenpodcast
description: The Law Queen Podcast, is a podcast dedicated to exploring the intricacies of personal injury law, with a focus on serious injury, wrongful death, and negligence cases. Hosted by Sean O'Connor, the show features in-depth conversations with legal experts like Nicole Lahmani, offering listeners a comprehensive understanding of the legal landscape. The series aims to demystify legal processes, providing practical insights and strategies for individuals navigating complex legal challenges. With a commitment to clarity and compassion, The Law Queen Podcast serves as a valuable resource for anyone seeking to understand their rights and the pursuit of justice in personal injury cases.

title: The Good Side of Sports Podcast
author: Brian Hartong
description: The Good Side of Sports Podcast highlights the good being done by athletes and organizations and all the amazing ways they are giving back. Join us as we talk with some of the biggest names in sports as well as incredible sports teams and foundations. You will be inspired by their passion for the causes they support and may even be moved to join in helping support those causes. Remember to "Show your good side out there everyone".

title: Mugada Siva Ganesh
author: Mugada Siva Ganesh
description:
Hey, I’m Mugada Siva Ganesh — trader, investor, entrepreneur, and author. I’ve spent years navigating both the financial markets and the realities of building businesses from the ground up.
On this channel, I share perspectives and frameworks across equities, crypto, decision-making, risk, mindset, long-term value creation, and more.
If you’re focused on building something meaningful — whether it’s financial independence, a business, or a stronger version of yourself — you’ll find something here worth your time.

title: Headline: HIV
author: Dan Hall
description: Brought to you by the podcast 'HIV: The Morning After', these are headlines from the world of HIV in three minutes or less.

title: The Gate Post Podcast
author: Arizona Cattle Growers Association
description: Welcome to Ranchers for Tomorrow: The Gate Post, the official podcast of the Arizona Cattle Growers Association. Join host Nate Brawley as he shares conversations with Arizona ranchers, industry leaders, and advocates about the people, policies, and traditions shaping the future of the state's beef industry. From stories on the ranch to updates from the association, each episode celebrates the heritage, resilience, and innovation driving Arizona cattle ranching forward.

title: Prototype
author: Gavin Liu
description: Prototype exists to close one distance: the space between the people building the future and the people who back them. It is made for founders and investors, and for anyone drawn to technology, to innovation, to the stubborn work of changing the world by building something real. In each episode, Gavin sits down with a founder working at the frontier, on how technology actually gets built, how a direction gets corrected, and how conviction holds through the days when no one believes in you.

title: Life Swerves With Dr. Tangela
author: Dr. Tangela Harris
description: Welcome to life wives with Dr. Tangela, the podcast for everyone navigating unexpected turns in life. Through real stories, biblical wisdom, and practical strategies, Dr. Tangela helps you recognize life‘s detour without losing your direction. Whether you’re facing grief, loss, career change, relationship challenges, leadership, transition, or seasons of uncertainty, you’ll discover how to readjust, realign, and move forward with purpose. Remember: Clarity restores power. Alignment restores peace. Structure restores momentum. Your life swerve is not the end of your story.

title: Prayer Therapy
author: Samuel Charlotin
description: A Place Where We Can Have Conversation Walking Through The Emotions Of Everyday Life. We Aspire To Be A Community Of People Who Love The Lord And Are Vulnerably Rooted In Him.

title: LabourList Podcast
author: LabourList
description:
LabourList provides the leading dedicated forum for authoritative news, insightful analysis and robust debate about the Labour Party across the UK, through our website, social media, daily newsletter and events.
Our readers, contributors and speakers alike come from across the party and beyond it, from cabinet ministers, backbenchers, councillors and members to experts, journalists and campaigners.
Launched in 2009, we are supportive of the Labour Party, but independent of it and see ourselves as a “honest friend”.

title: Do you have kids? Short answer: No.
author: Lindsay Bane
description: A collection of personal stories from women who identify as Childless Not By Choice, for people of the CNBC community and for people who want to learn about the CNBC experience.
